summary: Finds the position of a scene in the SceneOrder list: initializes this[3] (offset 0xC) to 0x7FFFFFFF as a sentinel, invokes AudioChannelStop with the game-data global and the "SceneOrder" name, computes the scene entry address as dword_8AC490 + 396 * this[0] (offset 0x0), and when the entry is non-null scans the SceneOrder list comparing each node name against the entry's name at offset 260. On the first matching node it stores the node index into this[3]; it stops early returning null when the list is exhausted. Return value varies by path.

local_names.v3: current SceneOrder list node index, incremented while scanning
local_names.v5: scene name pointer at scene entry + 260
local_names.v6: name string pointer of the current SceneOrder list node
local_names.result: current list node pointer / name-comparison outcome

operations.description: this[3] = 0x7FFFFFFF; initialize the stored slot position at offset 0xC to the maximum sentinel.
AudioChannelStop(dword_8AD3B4, aSceneorder); invoke with the game-data global dword_8AD3B4 and the "SceneOrder" name string constant.
v4 = dword_8AC490 + 396 * this[0]; compute the scene entry address from the array base dword_8AC490 using this[0] (offset 0x0) as the scene index with a 396-byte stride.
If v4 (the scene entry) is non-null, proceed with the scan; otherwise skip it and fall through to the final return.
result = NullCheckWrapper(0); retrieve the first SceneOrder list node by index 0.
If the first list node is null, skip the scan.
v5 = v4 + 260; point at the scene name field of the scene entry.
Scan the SceneOrder list nodes starting at index 0, advancing v3 each iteration, until a name match is found or the list ends.
v6 = StringPointerAccessor(result); extract the name string pointer from the current list node.
result = sub_588410(v6, v5); compare the node name against the scene name; a zero/null result is treated as the match.
If the comparison result is null (match found), break out of the loop.
result = NullCheckWrapper(++v3); advance the index and fetch the next list node.
If the next node is null (list exhausted), return null immediately.
this[3] = v3; store the matching node index at offset 0xC, replacing the sentinel.
